problems.title: The moment inequality needs a mixed-term condition
problems.source_location: Lemma B.1, PDF p.15; actual use in Lemma B.2, pp.15–16
claim: The statement claims \(\|X+Y\|_p^2\le\|X\|_p^2+(p-1)\|Y\|_p^2\) for arbitrary finite-moment random vectors.
analysis: At \(p=2\), deterministic \(X=Y=1\) requires \(4\le2\). Even centered equal Rademacher variables give the same failure. The mixed inner product need not vanish. A sufficient condition is \(\mathbb E[Y\mid\mathcal G]=0\) with \(X\) measurable to \(\mathcal G\); the usual martingale smoothness inequality then applies. In Lemma B.2, the past iterate/drift is measurable and iid unbiased gradient noise is conditionally centered, exactly as the proof states.
result: The auxiliary statement is false, but its repaired actual application preserves the one-step recursion and Theorem 2.1 under the paper’s original assumptions.
repair: Add conditional centering to the lemma. For its SGD application, identify the past sigma-algebra explicitly; no change to the main recursion is required.

problems.title: Vanishing steps alone need not remove accumulated noise
claim: The isolated remark says the exploration sum is \(o(1)\) when \(\eta_n\to0\).
analysis: For \(f(\theta,\xi)=(\theta-\xi)^2/2\), independent Rademacher \(\xi\), start at optimum \(0\), use \(p=2,\mu=L_2=M_2=1,c_0=1,\eta_t=0.1\,2^{-t}\). The theorem’s step restrictions hold, but the first summand alone gives \(S_n\ge0.0025e^{-0.05}>0\). Actual variance also obeys \(v_n\ge0.0025\prod_{k=2}^n(1-\eta_k)^2\ge0.00225625\). Thus initialization removal does not cure the isolated criterion. Remark 2.1 separately discusses divergent accumulated steps, which may be the intended joint premise.
result: The isolated sufficiency statement needs qualification; the finite bound and separately analyzed Linear-D2Z result are not refuted.
repair: For a fixed infinite schedule, require both \(\eta_t\to0\) and \(\sum_t\eta_t=\infty\) with fixed \(c_0>0\). Splitting off finitely many early terms and bounding the tail by \( \delta e^{c_0M}/c_0\), \(M=\sup\eta_t\), proves convergence. Finite-horizon triangular arrays need their own uniform conditions.

problems.title: The plotting helpers exchange MSE and squared-error SD
claim: The statistic function returns named list \((\mathrm{se.sd},\mathrm{mse})\), but positional helpers label the first MSE and second SD.
analysis: Three error vectors \((0,0),(3,4),(0,0)\) have squared errors \(0,25,0\), mean \(25/3\) and sample SD \(25/\sqrt3\). Returned list order therefore labels approximately \(14.4338\) as MSE and \(8.3333\) as SD; both center and ribbon are exchanged. Names do not reverse R insertion order.
result: The released plotting map is incorrect. The statistic producer itself is correct, and actual provenance of every published figure remains unestablished; no native R run occurred in this check.
repair: Extract the mse and se.sd fields by name in both helpers, then regenerate affected figures from run-level errors or saved statistic objects.

problems.title: The Figure 1 script averages norms rather than squared norms
problems.source_location: Figure 1 and Section 3.2, PDF p.7; section_3_2_plot_1.R, mse.lr.linear.schedule
claim: The script returns \(\sqrt{\sum_j(\theta_j-\theta_j^\star)^2}\) before averaging, under an MSE label.
analysis: Errors \((0,0),(3,4)\) yield mean norm \(2.5\), MSE \(12.5\), and RMSE \(\sqrt{12.5}\), all distinct. Squaring the mean norm gives \(6.25\), which cannot recover MSE. An \(O(n^{-1/2})\) MSE bound only gives \(O(n^{-1/4})\) mean norm by Jensen, so the released statistic cannot directly validate the stated MSE rate.
result: The local metric is mislabeled or miscomputed. The theorem remains independent, and this script has not been authenticated as the exact source of the published figure.
repair: Return squared norms for MSE, or relabel the statistic and revise its theoretical comparison. Recover run-level errors rather than squaring an aggregate mean.
